title: The yard at Muileann chrom goes to a double shift
summary: The yard at Muileann chrom takes on a double shift of drivers and firemen for the arms trains west, running by night as well as by day. Eachann mac Ruairidh is given the run, and told to sign the manifest for weight and ask nothing of the goods.

title: The first sealed wagons loaded at Muileann chrom
summary: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's own men load eight wagons behind tarpaulin at Muileann chrom by shuttered lamp, and take the loading out of the yard drivers' hands for the first time in the line's history.

title: The western branch runs arms by night
summary: Through am Faoilleach Slighe a' Ghuail's western branch, laid twenty years before for lime and slate, carries arms and dubhan west to Seann Bhral by night, at speeds the branch's rails were never built to bear.

title: Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's quay at Seann Bhral
summary: At Seann Bhral Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's men unload the arms trains by lantern into a lorry kept always waiting, and give the driver nothing for his signature but a bare manifest.

title: A company passes the arms train below the capital
summary: One of the new-raised companies, marching west by night under a corporal Eachann mac Ruairidh had once carried as a passenger, passes below the arms train on the branch road and is not stopped for.

title: A Tuathach family on the western branch
summary: Eachann mac Ruairidh's train passes a Tuathach family walking north along Slighe a' Ghuail's western branch before dawn, a handcart between them. He does not stop, and does not look back.

title: Cnoc thais comes to Àth leathan
summary: Tom Varley leads forty hewers and more of Cnoc thais down the ridge drove track to Àth leathan, pit-lamps lit at noon though no face waits at the path's end to work by them.

title: Àth naomh comes to Àth leathan
summary: The hewers of Àth naomh come to Àth leathan marching two abreast, keeping their own order at another town's pit-head though they have nothing there yet to defend.

title: Muileann àrsaidh and Tobar dhearg of the hills come to Àth leathan
summary: Smaller parties from Muileann àrsaidh and from Tobar dhearg of the hills reach Àth leathan through a second cold dusk, among them boys of fourteen and, from two houses, whole households with none left at home.

title: Ruth Calder's list begun at the pit-shed
summary: Ruth Calder sets up a trestle table at the Àth leathan pit-shed and takes down every man's and boy's name, town by town, with a mark for those who bring their own tools.

title: Sarah Dunmore sends oatmeal to Àth leathan
summary: Sarah Dunmore sends two cartloads of oatmeal and a barrel of salted fish down from Muileann àrsaidh for the gathering at Àth leathan, and asks no thanks for it.

title: Ruth Calder learns Comhairle nam Mèinnean keeps its own list
summary: Tom Varley brings word to Ruth Calder that Comhairle nam Mèinnean at Cathair mhòr keeps a list of its own, with her name and his set above every other on it.

title: The pit-sheds and byres given over at Àth leathan
summary: The three pit-sheds of Àth leathan fill with sleeping men on straw, and the byres behind the chapel, their cattle turned out, hold the rest.

title: The regiments set out from Cathair dhearg
summary: On the three-and-twentieth of am Faoilleach the regiments set out from Cathair dhearg by the western road, their lorries running on dubhan the length of the column, bound for the enforcers' quarters at Seann Skell in the west.

title: The regiments camp beside the enforcers at Seann Skell
summary: The regiments from Cathair dhearg reach the western Seann Skell and camp beside the enforcers already quartered there, three years settled and waiting for exactly this company.

title: Word of the march reaches Àth leathan
summary: A carter carries word up from the boundary stones to Àth leathan that the regiments have gone west by the road below Cathair dhearg, their lorries running on dubhan.

title: Signed for weight and not for goods
summary: The yard foreman at Muileann chrom hands Eachann mac Ruairidh a manifest giving only the weight of eight sealed wagons, and he is not to ask what is in them.

title: Lamps lit at noon on the hill paths
summary: The hewers of the five towns come down to Àth leathan with their pit-lamps lit at noon, so that every farm in the western hills sees them come as pit men.

title: Tobar dhearg's captain sets his lamp on the table
summary: The stooped captain of Tobar dhearg of the hills sets his lamp on Ruth Calder's trestle table before he gives his own name.

title: Four hundred names by the sixth evening
summary: By the sixth evening of the gathering Ruth Calder's list at Àth leathan runs past four hundred men and boys of the five towns.
